newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice mostly steady, Malaysia buys - traders.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice mostly steady, Malaysia buys - traders.

text.p: Preparations for rice shipments to meet purchases by the Philippines and Malaysia were the key features in a steady Thai market this week, trade sources said on Thursday.
Rice prices were mostly steady while top quality fragrant rice continued to spiral upward on China and Hong Kong liftings, they told Reuters.
Malaysia bought 10,000 tonnes of 100 percent B grade rice through a recent tender at US$345 per tonne tonne FOB Bangkok, they said.
The market was still trying to get confirmation on a report that a Malaysia trading firm, MITCO Petronas, inked a deal to sell 100,000 tonnes of optional origin rice to the Philippines.
"This is an interesting report. I have not heard of it so far from my sources there but I'm not saying that it is impossible," said a trader from a firm which regularly sells rice to Malaysia.
Malaysia is a net rice importer and normally buys good quality rice such as 100 percent grade from Thailand for local consumption while the Philippines buys mostly 25 percent grade.
"If the report is confirmed, Malaysia will definitely have to import rice from other countries to meet the obligation," the trader said.
"But I am not sure if (Malaysia) will find our lower grade rice prices attractive. I guess we will find that out pretty soon," he added.
Other orders came from regular customers like Singapore and the United States. Traders were disappointed that most African clients, dismayed by high Thai prices, had turned to India and Pakistan.
Thai exporters will start loading about 55,000 tonnes of 25 percent grade rice as the first shipment to the Philippines beginning next week.
This is a part of a 205,000-tonne shipment that Manila bought from Thailand on a government-to-government basis for March/April and May/June shipments at $300 per tonne.
"I hope the lifting won't push the price up much as most exporters have already covered their positions," said a local trader.
At ports, ships were loading around 118,000 tonnes of rice for deliveries, including 13,000 tonnes to Iraq, 13,500 to Malaysia, 13,000 to China and 6,000 to Hong Kong.
